facts.statement: A policy, application, rider or endorsement delivered in New Jersey that does not comply with Title 17B is interpreted as if it did comply.
facts.quote: shall be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements and shall be interpreted by the courts and among the persons affected by the policy or contract as if that policy or contract form were in compliance with the requirements

items.stem: A life policy delivered in New Jersey contains a provision less favorable to the policyowner than state law requires. How is the policy interpreted?
options: As written, since the owner accepted it
As void, with all premiums refunded
As written until the commissioner orders a change
As if it complied with the law
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-18.1 provides that a policy delivered in New Jersey that does not comply with Title 17B is deemed to comply and is interpreted as if it did, without relieving the insurer of any penalty.

facts.statement: A policy form filed with the commissioner is deemed approved 60 days after submission unless disapproved in writing within that time.
facts.quote: shall be deemed approved upon the expiration of 60 days after the submission of the form unless disapproved in writing by the commissioner within that time

items.stem: An insurer files a new life policy form with the New Jersey commissioner. If the commissioner does not disapprove it in writing, the form is deemed approved after:
options: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-18.2(b) deems a filed form approved 60 days after submission unless the commissioner disapproves it in writing within that time.

facts.statement: Treating a noncomplying form as compliant does not relieve the insurer of any penalty for the violation.
facts.quote: except that this provision shall not relieve the insurer from any penalty that may be imposed for violation of this act

items.stem: A New Jersey insurer delivers a policy that does not comply with Title 17B, so the policy is read as if it complied. What is the effect on the insurer?
options: It is excused from any penalty
It may cancel the policy to cure the violation
It may still be penalized for the violation
It is excused if it reissues the policy
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-18.1 reads a noncomplying policy as if it complied, but that does not relieve the insurer from any penalty for the violation.

facts.statement: A policy on another person's life must benefit the insured, the insured's personal representative, or someone with an insurable interest when the contract was made.
facts.quote: or to a person having, at the time when that contract was made, an insurable interest in the individual insured

items.stem: For a policy on another person's life to be valid in New Jersey, when must the beneficiary's insurable interest exist?
options: When the contract is made
When the insured dies
Both at issue and at death
Throughout the life of the policy
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-1.1 requires the benefits to be payable to someone who had an insurable interest at the time the contract was made. It need not exist at death.

facts.statement: An individual has an insurable interest in a close relative by blood or by law in whom he has a substantial interest engendered by love and affection.
facts.quote: (3) An individual has an insurable interest in the life, health and bodily safety of another individual to whom he is closely related by blood or by law and in whom he has a substantial interest engendered by love and affection.

items.stem: Under New Jersey law, which of the following has an insurable interest in Ana's life without having to show any financial interest in her?
options: Ana's adult sister
Ana's landlord
Ana's next-door neighbor
Ana's former classmate
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-1.1 gives an insurable interest to a person closely related by blood or by law who has a substantial interest engendered by love and affection. Friends, neighbors and coworkers would need a financial interest.
